residue.text: Omitted fallback from stage1 and ATT: attended handback is an intervention hypothesis sacrificing self-service convenience. It may prevent unwatched mixing while adding queues and changing attention. Measure waiting and staffing feasibility; no success or causal discrimination is established.

Omitted historical details: tray one had two short counts, trays four and six one each, and every tray also recorded complete returns. Recurrence does not establish a tray defect. Original count accuracy, recovered-counter ownership, unresolved location, and closing-time concentration remain unknown.

Omitted limits: no new anomaly in one block leaves H1 and H2 unresolved; independent agreement can share error. Changed attention or compliance can mimic intervention benefit. These are retained hypotheses and limitations, not fabricated discarded observations.

summary.text: Synthetic record: four of eighteen first return counts were eleven; three later mat supplements restored twelve without witnessed origins. Three anomalies occurred near closing. Rounded counts and unwatched placements establish neither delayed borrower completion nor redistribution. Retain both branches through final selection.

H1 hypothesis: the selected borrower supplies the delayed twelfth counter. Prediction: a watched borrower-origin arrival precedes search or volunteer transfer, followed by independently agreed recovery. H2 competing hypothesis: another loan or volunteer supplies it. Prediction: recovery follows a witnessed other-loan or volunteer move without borrower completion. Either supports only that event; unwatched recovery selects neither.

Stage1 and INV intervention hypothesis: prospectively select ordinary and direct-to-own-tray self-service returns sequentially; hold intended demand and eligibility fixed, recording deviations. Preserve full five-minute loans. One volunteer watches transfer order; the second separately counts before movement. Log placement seconds, borrower arrivals, shortage reports, searches, transfers, mat counts, active loans, waiting, and time remaining; inspect at most one tray.

Retain H3 count-error hypothesis: independent disagreements or twelve without transfer favor counting uncertainty; agreed twelve at checkout then eleven weakens pure error but cannot exclude shared mistakes. INV reversed-arrow hypothesis: shortage reports trigger redistribution and apparent recovery. Pressure causing both hurried counts and handling is another hypothesis; temporal association alone proves neither.

Separately verify candidate kits: seventy-one counters permit at most five complete kits plus eleven. Issue only twelve, account for remainder, and clarify circulating versus simultaneously ready availability. Keep the return area usable; buy or mark nothing. Count at placement and one, three, five minutes when feasible. Record transfers before supplementation; replenishment proves no origin. A five-minute unresolved shortage fails reconciliation; earlier block ending leaves follow-up incomplete. Twenty minutes and forty volunteer-minutes bound this unproven outcome.
